reporting-org.narrative: CHRISTIAN AGENCY FOR PEACE AND DEVELOPMENT (CAPaD)

title.narrative: The Young Women For Awareness Agency Advocacy Accountability (YW4A) Programme, South Sudan

description.narrative: Strengthening the advocacy capacity up to 27 women's rights organizations to amplify young women's voices in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya and South Sudan by 2025. Enhancing the leadership of 13,700 young women to effectively engage in collective actions and decision making in public, private and civic spaces in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya and South Sudan by 2025. Transforming social norms and practices of 18 faith-based organizations (FBOs) that constraints young women's rights in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya and South Sudan by 2025. Influence the adaptation, amendment, withdrawal or effective utilization and implementation of 21 laws and policies towards promoting young women's rights to leadership, participation and ending SGBV in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya and South Sudan by 2025.

name.narrative: Juba, Yei, Terekeka, Yambio and Mundri

description.narrative: Juba, Yei and Terekeka are in Central Equatoria state of South Sudan and Yambio and Mundri are in the Western state

title.narrative: WRGE 5.2.2 (WRG049y) IO2 Strengthened individual leadership of 13, 700 young women

description.narrative: This indicator refers to the number of young women who are trained TOT and who experience changes in leadership skills, experiences and practices. Leadership roles are measured by capacity to apply different forms of leadership training (to peers), willingness to become role models, self-confidence and efficacy, planning and facilitation skills, public speaking, advocacy, willingness to engage in policy change and with actors in public and civic decision-making spaces, exercise of leadership roles in the community, women’s groups, CSOs and political spaces, mobilization of young women, networking.

title.narrative: WRGE 5.2.2 (WRG049y) # of young women who have gained awareness of their rights, deepened their understanding of women's rights issues, and the ability to generate support around a common cause.

description.narrative: This indicator refers to the number of young women who are trained TOT and who experience changes in leadership skills, experiences and practices.

comment.narrative: The total endline target for South Sudan has not changed following the MTR, and is set at 3,000 young women. Based on the actuals achieved so far, to reach the endline target in South Sudan at least 1,120 young women should be trained in RiseUp! during 2024.Despite facing administrative challenges that could hinder reaching the remaining target, the strategy is to focus on empowering young women in post-secondary institutions, leveraging the controlled environment of schools for effective engagement and empowerment.

In South Sudan, the programme was halted for a couple of months in 2024 and as a result the RiseUp! Leadership trainings were also on hold for a longer period. Once the YW4A programme resumed, efforts have been put on re-engaging previously trained young women, and identifying new cohorts. The final data on 2024 shows that in 2024, 331 (instead of 327) young women started with the RiseUp! training, which will continue throughout the first six months of 2025, as well as new young women will be identified and trained. The totals of previous years missed an additional 2 young women, which for the ease of IATI reporting are included in the 2024 numbers, resulting in the # of 333 YW reported upon this year. So far, South Sudan has reached a total of 2,205 out of the targeted 3,000 young women In 2024, 327 young women started with the RiseUp! training, which will continue throughout the first six months of 2025, as well as new young women will be identified and trained. Apart from Rise Up! and other training opportunities, the consortium prioritized initiatives to build young women's leadership skills and confidence through mentorship and platforms to engage with high-level decision-makers. For instance, young leaders were actively involved in various high-level forums, not just as participants but also as panelists and moderators. In 2024, they played key roles in platforms such as Beijing +30, the Human Rights Council 56th session (HRC), and the Sexual Violence Research Initiative (SVRI), showcasing their leadership and advocacy on global stages.
The total endline target for South Sudan is set at 3,000 young women, meaning that in 2025 at least 801 young women should be trained in RiseUp! during 2025 to achieve this target.

In the final year of YW4A, an additional 159 young women were trained in the RiseUp! Leadership programme. In total 2,364 young women were trained during the implementation period. This falls short of the target set for STO 2.1 in South Sudan (3,000) , and represents an achievement percentage of almost 80%. Ongoing insecurity in some target communities limited access to project locations such as Ezo, Mundri in Western Equatoria and restricted movement of staff and volunteers. This led to the postponement or scaling down of several planned activities. this was coupled with rising transportation costs due to economic constraints limited mobility to other project location.

title.narrative: WRGE 5.2.1 (WRG045, WRG047, WRG048) I01 Enhanced capacity of 16-28 WROs to amplify young women's voices

description.narrative: Under IO1 YW4A focuses on enhancing the organizational and advocacy capacity of a selected group of women's rights organizations. The programme also envisages amplifying young women’s voices by promoting that WROs provide space in their internal organisations for young women and establish internal inclusive processes and practices in decision-making, management, and programming. And by working with WROs to include, represent, hear, mentor, support, and prepare young women to take part in advocacy initiatives, link them to strategic decision-making forums, and scale-up local advocacy strategies

title.narrative: WRGE indicator 5.2.1 (WRG047): # of WROs with enhanced capacity to advance young women’s rights to bodily integrity and equal participation in decision-making.

comment.narrative: In South Sudan YW4A targets a total of 5 WROs under IO1. Deviations across the participating organizations are reported upon under targets.

There was a change in leadership of Pathway 1 in South Sudan (from YWCA South Sudan to CAPaD). Two of the three WROs engaged in the programme opted to continue under the new leadership. As a result from 2024 onwards, there are a total of 3 organizations engaged. YW4A decided not to onboard additional new WROs to achieve the initial target given limitations in light of the remaining timeframe.

During 2024, the YW4A programme in South Sudan was on hold for about six months. Following the MoFA-approved audit, it was agreed that the collaboration with the YWCA South Sudan, the original Country Lead, should be discontinued. The faith-based organization CAPaD, which had been engaged since the start of YW4A, was willing to take up the Country Lead position. During this period, the majority of activities – especially the trainings under the different pathways – were also paused. While some of the advocacy work was able to continue, leveraging on Equality Now partnerships and platforms in South Sudan, such as the Solidary for African Women’s Rights (SOAWR) coalition, to ensure the young women continued to learn and engage in legal advocacy processes and opportunities.
During 2025, YW4A continues to target the same WROs (those that take part since the start and new WROs that replaced initial selected WROs).

In its final year of implementation, the YW4A continued to work with the 3 remaining partners in South Sudan (2 WROs and 1 FBO). YW4A continued to build the capacity of these organizations, for example through M&E training, as well as (refresher) advocacy trainings and, equipping young women and organizations with skills to engage policymakers effectively, and contributing to increased participation in legal and policy reforms. There was also strong emphasize on networking and coalition building to advocate for young women’s rights, policy and legal changes jointly with other organizations.The final year also focused on the different endline studies, including conducting the Advocacy and Organizational Capacity Assessment (AOCA). At endline, the AOCA-reassessment and reflection workshop was conducted with the 3 organizations in South Sudan, to capture potential changes in their capacity and quantitative AOCA measures compared to baseline and mid-term. Out of the three remaining organizations in South Sudan, all (100%) have moved up at least one capacity level on the 7-point AOCA scale, meaning that in South Sudan the YW4A has met its outcome 1 indicator target. One of the organizations moved up one level, and the other two organizations even moved up two levels.
